title: add-hands-on-rag-playground-with-step-sequencer-and-telemetry-quickstart
author: Sofia Ramirez
release_notes: Adds a compact, hands-on RAG playground with a step sequencer UI, structured-output linter, lightweight telemetry probes, and a devcontainer for local iteration.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a self-contained RAG quickstart intended for engineers and developer advocates who want a reproducible, minimal playground for step-by-step instruction sequencing, assertable structured outputs, and lightweight telemetry probes. Motivation: teams repeatedly asked for a compact example that demonstrates: 1) authoring a stepwise retrieval+generation flow; 2) deterministically exercising tool calls; 3) validating structured responses during local dev; and 4) collecting minimal telemetry slices for early performance and quality checks. This quickstart is intentionally small (single-page dev app + CLI runner + sample corpus) to make it easy to fork and extend.

What changed (high-level):
- New quickstart directory: quickstarts/rag-step-sequencer
- Lightweight browser-based playground (React) that runs a step sequencer UI and a local in-memory retriever
- A small CLI harness (Node) to run the same workflows headless for CI/evals
- Structured-output linter for JSON schema checks with sample schemas and failing examples
- Telemetry probes: token-level timing and step-level success/failure counters emitted to a simple file sink for local inspection
- Devcontainer and README with step-by-step onboarding and suggested evaluation prompts

Checklist:
- [x] Minimal working UI and headless CLI
- [x] Sample corpus (5 documents) and embeddings pre-seeded for speed
- [x] Structured-output linting integrated into CLI and CI smoke job
- [x] Devcontainer and run instructions
- [x] Automated smoke test in CI that runs the CLI against the sample corpus

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The in-memory retriever uses a tiny vector index for quick bootstrapping; it is explicitly not production-grade. We document migration paths to the Redwood SDK-backed retriever in the README.
- The structured-output linter is schema-first (JSON Schema) and is intentionally permissive (warnings for soft constraints) so the example is friendly for experiments.
- Telemetry is intentionally minimal (file sink + example parsing script) to avoid telemetry ingestion cost and to give teams a starting point for wiring to Console.

- (ENG-4128) add an example that wires the telemetry sink to Redwood Console traces (next PR)

How to try it locally (concise):
1) git clone && cd quickstarts/rag-step-sequencer
2) code . (or open devcontainer)
3) npm ci && npm run dev to start playground; or npm run cli -- --seed 42 to run headless
4) check telemetry/telemetry.json for step timings and smoke results
